simple.meaning: אֵשֶׁל (ʼêshel) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a tamarisk tree ; by extension, a grove of any kind.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 21:33. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֵשֶׁל (H815) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אֵשֶׁל (ʼêshel) / H815 is traced through Genesis 21:33, 1 Samuel 22:6, 1 Samuel 31:13 with generated occurrence evidence.

structuredEvidence.definition: a tamarisk tree ; by extension, a grove of any kind

firstOccurrence.englishText: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and called there on the name of Yahweh, the Everlasting God.

timeline.evidenceText: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and called there on the name of Yahweh, the Everlasting God.

Saul heard that David was discovered, with the men who were with him. Now Saul was sitting in Gibeah, under the tamarisk tree in Ramah, with his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing around him.
They took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk

definitions.full: H815. eshel אֵ֫שֶׁל noun masculine tamarisk-tree (Arabic , Sabean אתֿל SabDenkm 65 compare DHM BS ii. 958 ; on an Aramaic אַתְלָא see Löw No. 38 ; compare Tristr FFP 250 ) planted by Abraham Gen 21:33 (J); in 1Sam 22:6 Saul is dwelling בָּרָמָה תַּחַתהָֿאֵשֶׁל בַּגִּבְעָה ; 31:13 Saul and his sons are buried ׳תַּחַתהָֿא ; it was perhaps a sacred tree, marking shrine.
